files.description: Bike-share trips, 1 September to 1 November 2025 (1500 rows): trip_id (whole number), rider_id (refers to riders.csv), start_station and end_station (refer to station_code in stations.csv), started_at (timestamp written as YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM), duration_min (whole minutes; about 3% empty), distance_km (two decimals), fare (two decimals; about 3% empty), payment (card, app or cash; capital letters and spaces are inconsistent), rating (1-5 stars, whole number; about 19% empty).

Bike-share stations (48 rows, one per station): station_code (four-digit code with leading zeros, e.g. "0040"), station_name (text, a few with accented letters), district (same 6 districts as riders.csv; capital letters and spaces are inconsistent), docks (whole number), opened_on (date as text, YYYY-MM-DD).

task_text: Use stations.csv as a lookup from station_code to docks and replace every station code in the start_station and end_station columns of trips.csv by the docks of that station; a code that does not appear in stations.csv stays as it is. `result` should be a table with the columns start_station and end_station, one row per trip.
intended_computation: Read trips.csv and stations.csv; map every start_station and end_station code through station_code -> docks (all codes are found); columns start_station, end_station holding docks numbers; 1500 rows.

acceptable_variants.notes: values may be int, float or text digits; row order free

intent_summary: Replace the codes held in two columns of one table by the value that a second table gives for each code (code column to value column), leaving codes without a match as they are.
